answer: A ledge holds few by design. An identity may stand only on a ledge whose vertex two holders outside its own face attest, and each ledge admits one newcomer per epoch, so n aliases need n distinct ledges and n distinct attestors rather than one friendly ring. Occupying a ledge burns an ember whose price doubles with every occupant already present, so the k-th claim costs two to the k in bond and a coordinated swarm pays exponentially. An ember audit re-walks a random vertex; if the attested edge cannot be replayed, the entire ledge is cleared and its bonds forfeit.
